text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. Most APIs use HTTP requests to send and receive data, and the responses usually come in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key or token, to prove your identity. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, good error handling helps you deal with problems like network failures or invalid responses, so your application stays reliable and user-friendly.
